correctness.rationale: For a block not containing v, distance is 2 iff the block is the singleton mate of v; otherwise it is 1. In the same block, distinct vertices therefore collide exactly when neither mate is singleton. For s singleton blocks among k blocks, each nonsingleton block of size r needs at least r−1 distinct singleton mates, so s≥2n−k. Equality k=n would make all blocks singleton and leave vertices uncovered. With k=n+1, s is n or n−1. In the first case the one size-n block has at most one endpoint from each pair (an internal pair would create two exceptions), hence is a transversal; its complement gives the singleton blocks. In the second case tightness forces exactly one exception in each of the two large blocks and requires all singleton vertices to have nonsingleton mates. The exceptions must be mated across the two blocks, leaving the remaining n−1 mates to distribute with both blocks receiving one. These forms are sufficient by the same distance criterion. Canonically naming a large block by which endpoint of the exceptional pair it contains avoids a spurious division by two, giving 2^n+n2^(n−1)(2^(n−1)−2) on labeled vertices with unordered blocks; ordering multiplies by (n+1)!. The finite independent replay `python3 /workspace/branches/independent-checks.py 2` enumerated restricted-growth strings for n=3,4,5 (203,4140,115975 partitions) and tested distance vectors, giving optimum values 4,5,6 and counts 32,208,1152. This corroborates, but does not replace, the proof for n≥3. Read the frozen checker and expected output without executing the uploaded code.
